report.body_markdown:
# Research Report

**Goal:** Compare hybrid RAG, GraphRAG, and long-context retrieval architectures for a production knowledge assistant in 2026. Evaluate retrieval quality, provenance, update cost, operational complexity, latency, security, evaluation strategy, and the workloads for which each architecture is most appropriate. Prefer original papers and official framework or vendor documentation.

## Questions
- (answered) Investigate Hybrid RAG architectures (dense vector + BM25/SPLADE sparse search + rerankers), analyzing retrieval precision/recall, latency, update workflows, chunking/provenance tracking, and multi-tenant access control.
- (answered) Investigate GraphRAG architectures (entity extraction, graph construction, hierarchical Leiden clustering, community summaries), analyzing multi-hop synthesis, index building/update costs, latency, provenance, and RBAC support.
- (answered) Investigate Long-Context retrieval architectures, evaluating context-window retrieval fidelity, prompt caching latency and cost economics, context updating mechanisms, and granular document-level security limitations.
- (answered) Synthesize findings into an enterprise comparative evaluation matrix covering retrieval quality, provenance/auditability, update cost, operational complexity, latency/throughput, security/RBAC, evaluation strategies (e.g., Ragas, TruLens), and workload decision frameworks.

## Synthesis
Defer final architectural selection between Hybrid RAG, GraphRAG, and Long-Context retrieval architectures due to insufficient comparative benchmark and architectural evidence. In the interim, implement rigorous pre-ingestion data sanitization and defense-in-depth security controls against indirect prompt injection across any retrieval pipeline.

The available verified evidence addresses only generic data privacy and security considerations in retrieval pipelines—specifically highlighting the necessity of pre-filtering sensitive data prior to indexing and the inherent vulnerability where models process attacker-controlled text before detecting malicious instructions. There is currently insufficient verified evidence to evaluate or contrast Hybrid RAG, GraphRAG, and Long-Context retrieval systems across retrieval quality, provenance tracking, update overhead, operational complexity, latency, and specific 2026 workload archetypes.
